summary: EmberSearch (Dedicated): Dedicated pool upgrades need phased rollout with objective gates + fast rollback
description:
Account: EmberSearch (Dedicated)
Primary contacts: (via TAM) Head of Platform Eng + oncall rotation

Issue summary
Customer is requesting a safer, deterministic process for Dedicated pool upgrades (model version/runtime build/routing policy changes) using phased/staged rollouts with measurable gates and quick rollback. They explicitly do not want “big bang” pool flips.

Why this is urgent / escalation context
- EmberSearch runs embeddings + reranking traffic with strict latency SLOs and spiky batch workloads.
- They experienced customer-visible impact during the last 2 Dedicated pool upgrades.
- They have internal change management requirements (platform sign-off) and want a documented, auditable process.

Impact history (customer-reported)
1) 2024-12-11 (us-east): pool upgrade caused p99 latency to jump ~2.5x for ~25–35 minutes after cutover; intermittent 5xx; rollback required.
2) 2025-01-17 (multi-region): partial upgrade (us-east first, eu-west later) caused uneven routing and elevated 429s; they saw request drops during peak traffic. Customer’s take: “We couldn’t tell if this was capacity, routing, or the new build; we had no gating data and no safe ‘pause’ button.”

Customer request (what they want)
They are asking Redwood to provide (or document as an interim) a staged rollout workflow for a single Dedicated pool:
- Default stages: 1% → 10% → 50% → 100% (or replica partitions for small pools)
- Minimum time in stage: configurable (they suggested 30–60 minutes)
- Gate evaluation before promotion, with clear pass/fail reasoning
- Ability to HOLD (pause) a rollout and keep traffic pinned to the last good stage
- Fast abort/rollback that reverts routing immediately (with clarity on what happens to in-flight streams)
- Audit trail of actions (who promoted/overrode/aborted, reason, timestamps)

Desired gating metrics (customer-proposed)
Customer specifically asked for objective gates, visible in Console or exportable:
1) Error rate: 5xx + timeouts (HTTP and upstream), broken out by region and stage
2) Throttling: 429 rate and queue-depth / saturation indicators (they suspect last issue was capacity starvation)
3) Latency: p95 + p99 end-to-end, and (if possible) server-side tokenization/compute breakdown
4) GPU health: unhealthy nodes, ECC errors, throttling, GPU resets
5) OOM / memory pressure: OOM kill count, KV cache eviction pressure (if applicable)
6) Headroom: utilization/saturation gate to ensure the canary partition isn’t under-provisioned
7) (Nice-to-have) Quality regression checks: simple eval/prompt set or embedding drift sanity checks, at least for major version upgrades

Environment details
- Dedicated pool: ES-embed-prod (multi-region us-east + eu-west)
- Traffic pattern: spiky batch (indexing) + steady online traffic
- Peak QPS: customer reports 2–4x within 5 minutes during their indexing windows

Asks from Redwood (support request)
- Provide a near-term, operator-led staged upgrade procedure we can run for their next upgrade (even if manual gating).
- Provide a timeline/commitment for first-class “staged rollouts for Dedicated pools” so they can plan.
- Identify whether we can support replica-based stages when the pool is small (to avoid capacity fragmentation).

Internal notes / triage
This request aligns with the ongoing Dedicated staged rollouts project (rollout plans + stage gates + promote/abort/hold + audit logging + Console timeline). Customer is a strong candidate for design partner / beta.

Next scheduled customer touchpoint
- 2025-02-06: technical deep dive requested (TAM + SRE + Product) to walk through proposed stages, gate signals, and rollback semantics.
comments: 2025-01-29 09:12 PT - Liam O'Rourke (TAM): Logging per EmberSearch escalation. They want staged upgrades with gating + rollback. Last upgrade was painful and they’re requesting commitments before next quarterly upgrade window.

2025-01-31 14:22 PT - Sean Gallagher (SRE): Gate proposals should be tied to their SLO and error budget burn. We should also include a ‘no promote during incident/high burn’ rule. Missing metrics should fail-closed with manual override, otherwise we’ll ship a footgun.

2025-02-03 11:06 PT - Liam O'Rourke (TAM): Customer provided desired thresholds (informal): 5xx < 0.2%, p99 < 900ms, 429 < 0.5% during canary; wants 30m windows and ability to extend. They’re okay with Redwood-defined defaults as long as they can see what we’re evaluating and why we blocked a promote.

2025-02-06 13:35 PT - Lauren Bishop (PM, Dedicated): Completed technical deep dive with customer. We aligned on default stages (1/10/50/100) and documented HOLD + ABORT semantics. Action: we’ll enroll EmberSearch in limited beta once feature flag is available; interim workaround is operator-run canary using a separate shadow pool only for batch indexing traffic (not ideal).

2025-02-07 09:28 PT - Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Beta enablement will be behind feature flag; we can target a controlled enablement for 1–2 accounts after migrations. Please file an internal enablement request when ready (INT ticket).

2025-02-10 15:04 PT - Lauren Bishop (PM, Dedicated): Creating Product escalation notes: customer needs gate evidence visible in Console (not just internal dashboards) and audit trail export. Also requesting replica-based stages for small pools to avoid 429s from partition starvation.

2025-02-11 10:26 PT - Liam O'Rourke (TAM): Filed internal request to enable staged rollouts beta once available (linked INT-1933). Customer agrees to be design partner; wants a written runbook and a ‘go/no-go’ checklist for each promotion.

2025-02-12 16:50 PT - Rafael Mendes (SRE): Added EmberSearch to candidate list for beta with SRE monitoring plan. Recommendation: start with manual gates + strict hold/abort; do not allow auto-promote for first rollout. Ensure headroom validation (min replicas) to avoid a repeat of the 429 issue.
resolution: Resolved as product/enablement path: Confirmed alignment with Dedicated staged rollouts project. Customer accepted interim operator-led canary workaround for next upgrade window and agreed to join limited beta. Internal enablement tracking moved to INT-1933; follow-on capacity starvation investigation tracked separately (see SUP-28522 for early beta 429 behavior reference).
